plot: The evening after the pirate fuss, Bolt opens the box from 'an old friend': a silver star, a popcorn smell, wobbly writing and a drawing of a tiny laughing van, but he can't remember who it is; Turbo's famous-racer guess and Bertha's cousin guess fail, Pip stops him pretending, and at the old drive-in cinema at night the memory of a tiny purple van comes back, a rustle turns out to be a hedgehog, and near midnight huge Hal the moving truck arrives with his 'ho-ho-honk' laugh (heard early on) — he was little Hally, who grew up and moved away, and Bolt didn't recognise him; Hal stays in Wheelburg for good; lesson: faces change, friends stay; then a light blinks on in the old projector room.

script.title: Bolt Forgot His Oldest Friend?!

set.place: Bakery Lane at dusk, then the old drive-in cinema field at the edge of Wheelburg until midnight

script.description: A box from 'an old friend' and a detective who can't remember who sent it. Inspector Bolt #19

beats.say: A box for me? From an old friend? Which old friend?
Open it, Bolt! Open it! I can't wait!
It was the same evening. The street lights were just coming on.
Procedure. First we look. Then we open.
Brown paper. A smell of popcorn. And very wobbly writing.
Popcorn? Maybe it's a snack! Open it already!
Inside lay a little silver star. And a folded note.
Dear Bolt. I still have our promise. Do you?
Meet me where the big screen shows the stars. Tonight.
And at the bottom, a drawing. A tiny laughing van!
A promise? A star? I don't remember any of it.
But Bolt, you remember everything! Every single tyre track!
Every tyre track in Wheelburg. But not this friend.
Just then, Hal the moving truck rolled back down Bakery Lane.
Forgot my ramp straps! Evening, everyone! Ho-ho-honk!
Nobody looked up. Everybody was staring at the little star.
A big screen? That's the old drive-in cinema by the fields!
Closed for years. Weeds. Crickets. One big white wall.
I went there once. When I was a very small car.
But who did he go with? Bolt could not remember.
I know! It's Blaze McRev! The famous racing car!
Everybody wants to be his friend. Even me!
Turbo, I have never met a famous racing car.
Maybe you forgot that too! Vroom vroom!
Oh, stop it, Turbo. Famous cars don't draw little vans.
Bolt, maybe it's your cousin! Cousins always say old friend.
My cousin Cog is two years old. He can't write yet.
Two guesses. Two wrong. And the sky was getting darker.
My friend still has our promise. And I forgot it.
If I don't remember by tonight, my friend will feel forgotten.
So Bolt had an idea. A not very good idea.
I'll just say, Old pal! Of course I remember you!
Bolt! That's pretending. That's not the truth.
You're right, Pip. A detective never pretends.
Then stop guessing. Be a detective. Look at the clues.
Clue one. Popcorn. Clue two. Wobbly writing.
Wobbly like a car who writes while driving!
Clue three. A little van that laughs. Let's go.
So off they drove, out to the edge of Wheelburg.
The old drive-in. A field of crickets. A giant empty screen.
It's so quiet. Too quiet. Where's the popcorn?
Bolt parked right in front of the big white screen.
And slowly, very slowly, a memory came back.
I sat right here. Next to a tiny purple van.
He was smaller than Pip! And he laughed all night.
Smaller than me? Nobody is smaller than me!
We watched the stars. Then he had to move away.
I gave him my silver star. To keep until he came back.
No name. No friend. And midnight was coming fast.
Something rustled in the weeds. Everybody spun around.
A tiny van! It must be him! Hello, little friend!
That's a hedgehog, Bertha. A very surprised hedgehog.
Bertha laughed so hard her roof went flat.
The stars came out, one by one. Nobody else came.
It's almost midnight. Maybe my friend gave up on me.
Wait, Bolt. Look! Two great big headlights!
A huge truck rolled slowly across the field.
Hal? Did you forget your straps again?
No straps tonight. I came to meet an old friend.
Ho-ho-honk!
Bolt knew that laugh. He had heard it right here.
Hally? Little Hally? But you were tiny!
I grew up, Bolt. Quite a lot, really.
Yesterday you looked right at me. You said, Good afternoon, sir.
Oh, Hally. I'm so sorry. I didn't know it was you.
That's why I sent the star. And the popcorn smell.
And the wobbly writing! You wrote it while driving!
Bumpy roads. Movers write everywhere.
I moved homes for everybody. Now I want my own. Here.
Then our promise is kept. Welcome home, old friend.
Hmph. Fine. I brought popcorn. Just in case.
Grumpy switched on his work lights. The big screen glowed.
Shadow shapes! Look, I'm a giant hedgehog!
Remember, everyone. Faces change. Friends stay.
Faces change. Friends stay. I'll remember that!
Then, high in the old projector room, a light blinked on.
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!

"I remember every tyre track in Wheelburg. So how did I forget a friend?" — Inspector Bolt
A box arrives with a silver star, a popcorn smell and a note from "an old friend" — and Bolt can't remember who it is. Before the stars come out, he follows the clues to the old drive-in cinema. Inspector Bolt #19
